With the ridge mapper at its selected k (k = 20), Llama 3.1 8B→70B transfer reaches **57.78% on MMLU** and **14.78% on GSM8K** (Table 13, p. 18).

| | MMLU (5-shot) | GSM8K (8-shot CoT) |
|---|---|---|
| 8B→70B transfer, k=20 | **57.78** | **14.78** |
| 70B standalone (target) | 78.84 | 81.12 |
| 8B standalone (source) | 64.97 | 56.10 |
| Retention vs. 70B (Table 1, p. 6) | 73.3% | 18.2% |

- **Setup:** Table 1 (p. 6) gives the selected k for this pair as 20, using the ridge mapper in content space. Table 13 (p. 18) is the full version of Table 1 and lists raw accuracies. The benchmark settings (MMLU 5-shot, GSM8K 8-shot with chain-of-thought) are stated on p. 6.
- **Retention:** The percentages match the raw numbers: 57.78/78.84 ≈ 73.3% and 14.78/81.12 ≈ 18.2%.
- **What it means:** Transfer scores below the 8B model running alone on both benchmarks. GSM8K drops the most.
- **How k was chosen:** k was picked using ARC-C, HellaSwag, WinoGrande and MMLU. GSM8K was left out of that choice (p. 6). So the GSM8K number did not influence the selection. The paper says including a benchmark in the selection raises its own reported accuracy by at most 2.49 pp (p. 6).
